newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-BENGALS GRANT FOUR-YEAR CONTRACT EXTENSION TO COSLET.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-BENGALS GRANT FOUR-YEAR CONTRACT EXTENSION TO COSLET.

text.p: The Cincinnati Bengals Sunday extended the contract of head coach Bruce Coslet through the year 2000.

The announcement was made by Bengals president and general manager Mike Brown before Sunday's game at Houston, in which the Bengals posted a 21-13 victory that knocked the Oilers oiut of the AFC playoff race.
The contract will automatically extend to 2001 if the Bengals reach the playoffs in 1999 or 2000.
Cincinnati is 6-2 since Coslet was promoted from his offensive coordinator position to replace David Shula as head coach on October 21.
Coslet also served as Bengals offensive coordinator from 1986 to 1989 before becoming head coach of the New York Jets from 1990 to 1993.
Coslet was 26-39 as coach of the Jets, leading them to their last playoff appearance, a wild-card berth in 1991.
The 50-year-old Coslet played tight end for the Bengals from 1969 to 1976 and was on the coaching staff both seasons the Bengals won the AFC title (1981 and 1988).
